problem: Unified fusion of 2D images, 3D point clouds and text at the feature level needs large 2D-3D-text triple corpora that barely exist, and monolithic fusion blurs each modality's strengths and removes cross-verification. Image-text navigation agents that rely only on pixel cues fail on spatial-distance and direction ambiguities.
motivation: Embodied navigation needs both visual cues (textures, paintings, maps) and spatial geometry (distance, layout). Image-text and 3D-text models have complementary strengths, and high-quality data exists mainly as image-text or 3D-text pairs. So collaboration at the model level via text may be cheaper and more effective than joint feature-level fusion.
key_idea: A frozen pretrained 3D-text LLM describes the spatial-semantic structure in natural language, and this text is fed into the image-text navigation LLM's prompt, which is lightly fine-tuned on a small 2D-3D-text corpus (Cross-Modal Belief Alignment).
insight: Sharing 3D hypotheses as text without alignment fine-tuning hurts (ablation iii: R2R SR 63 vs 64 baseline, ScanQA ROUGE 35.7), while alignment fine-tuning gives R2R SR 69/SPL 62, so resolving conflicting beliefs is the crucial step. Model-level fusion beats feature-level fusion trained on the same small triple-modality data (ScanQA ROUGE 38.9 vs 31.7) and beats a training-free Qwen2.5-7B 'CEO' post-process alignment (R2R SR 59). Curriculum pretraining of the 3D-text model matters, since ScanQA METEOR rises from 8.39 to 14.5 across stages.
method: Separate pretraining: the image-text navigation agent (EVA-CLIP ViT-g + Vicuna-7B) is trained following NaviLLM, and the 3D-text model (Point-BERT + MLP projector + Vicuna-7B) is trained independently.

Progressive curriculum for the 3D-text model: Stage 1 trains only the projector on Cap3D (770K) object captions; Stage 2 trains only the LLM on 3D-FRONT (51K) scene description and spatial-relation QA; Stage 3 trains the encoder and projector on self-built real-scan R2R/ScanNet point-text pairs (73K).

Point-text data pipeline for stage 3: Florence-2 detects objects, SAM segments them, RGB-D with camera parameters is back-projected into per-object point clouds, and these are merged into a scene point cloud, following SpatialVLM.

Communication Interface: at each step the agent issues a task prompt to the 3D-text model, which returns a text hypothesis π_3D (up to 64 tokens) from the point cloud. This is inserted as a 'Spatial Information' field into the navigation agent's standard prompt.

Cross-Modal Belief Alignment fine-tuning: the 3D-text model and the navigation encoder/projector are frozen and only the navigation LLM is fine-tuned, using a small triple-modality corpus (R2R, CVDN, REVERIE, SOON, ScanQA, SQA3D sampled 4:1:2:1:1:1) for about 130 A100-hours.
Inference: the 3D-text model processes (p_t, L), and its text is passed to the navigation agent, which outputs the next viewpoint or stop; the same pipeline answers ScanQA/SQA3D questions.

setting.backbone: Vicuna-7B navigation agent (EVA-CLIP ViT-g/14, fine-tuned LLM) + frozen Vicuna-7B 3D-text model (Point-BERT encoder)
setting.training_data: Navigation agent pretrained NaviLLM-style; 3D-text model on Cap3D 770K, 3D-FRONT 51K, self-generated R2R/ScanNet point-text 73K; alignment on a small 2D-3D-text corpus of R2R/CVDN/REVERIE/SOON/ScanQA/SQA3D
setting.observation: RGB-D panoramic views plus point clouds (8192 points, 512 patches) built from RGB-D, and instruction text
setting.privileged: none stated (point clouds are built from the agent's RGB-D observations with camera parameters)

numbers.extra: lightweight alignment fine-tuning on small triple-modality corpus

results: CoNav (Vicuna-7B) reaches R2R val-unseen SR 69 / SPL 62, higher SPL than NavGPT-2 (FlanT5-11B, 61) though lower SR (72). It sets the best SPL on REVERIE (37.54 val, 36.16 test) and reports SOON SPL 30.0 / 27.2 over NaviLLM (29.2 / 26.3). On the CVDN test leaderboard it is 2nd in GP (7.98, behind SRVLN 8.19) but has the best SPL (0.14 vs 0.09 for NaviLLM).
limitations: Text descriptions of 3D lose and add noise relative to the raw geometry, and point clouds are downsampled and expensive.
The 3D-text model is trained on data generated with image-text models (Florence-2, SAM), which may pass on their biases; the system runs two 7B LLMs per step.
Evaluated only in indoor simulators with reconstructed point clouds, no real robot; SR does not always beat the best baselines (e.g. REVERIE SR, R2R SR vs NavGPT-2).
